_comment: The exact hooks block Shepherd merges into ~/.claude/settings.json (user scope).
Paths are substituted at install time; shown here with placeholders.
Schema verified against code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks and settings-reference, Claude Code 2.1.270, 2026-09-14.
PreToolUse:
- matcher is a regex; covers exactly the consequential tools (decision 5).
- runs before permission evaluation for every matching call, so the hook
itself pass-throughs (exit 0, no output) when the user's own allow rules
match or the session is in bypassPermissions/acceptEdits mode.
- timeout 900s: Claude Code's hook timeout is non-blocking (the tool call
proceeds when it fires), matching our card-expiry behavior (decision 3).
Notification:
- matcher idle_prompt fires only for the ~60s idle 'waiting for input'
nudge; permission_prompt notifications are deliberately NOT intercepted
because PreToolUse already owns permission cards.
- timeout 10: the nudge exchange must never wait on a user decision.
Stop:
- no matcher: Stop is not tool-scoped.
- fires when the main agent finishes responding, i.e. once per turn;
Shepherd records one run per turn from last_assistant_message
(docs: prefer it over the transcript, which is not guaranteed to
include the final message at Stop time on all versions).
- the hook always exits 0 with no output: we never block the stop
(stop_hook_active / the 8-consecutive-block override never apply).
- timeout 10: same reasoning as Notification.
Merge rules: entries whose command contains 'shepherd-hook' are ours.
Install appends/refreshes them; uninstall removes exactly those entries.
All other hooks and keys are preserved verbatim (key order included).
